unmapped_findings: Instrumented Charpy U-notch impact data for the 1.3Al,2 h steel (Fig. 7c): peak load P_m = 38.6 KN, crack-initiation energy E_i = 62.0 J, crack-propagation energy E_p = 21.0 J, and total KU2 = 83.0 J; impact toughness from the bar chart is 80 ± 3 J.

Charpy U-notch impact toughness KU2 of the 1.3Al,2 h steel was measured as approximately 80 ± 3 J, corresponding to an improvement of about 3.5 times compared to its as-quenched state (23 ± 2 J); this is ~23 % higher impact absorption energy than the 0Al,2 h steel.

Peak loads (P_M) for the 1.3Al steel occurred at a deflection of 2.55 mm, with crack propagation accelerating at ~3 mm; rapid fracture occurred near the specimen center without an obvious crack-arrest stage.

Impact fracture of the 1.3Al,2 h steel showed a shear fracture area of 42.9 % (vs 36.8 % for 0Al), with enhanced number and size of large/deep primary dimples, more prominent tearing ridges and greater overall surface roughness, indicating ductile void growth and coalescence combined with quasi-cleavage.

In the 1.3Al steel, secondary cracks and voids measuring 5–10 μm were observed 8–18 μm below the main crack in fracture-toughness specimens, interconnected by fine cracks coalescing into larger secondary cracks; crack paths showed frequent deflections.

EBSD KAM of the 1.3Al steel near the impact fracture surface averaged 1.31° (matrix value 0.79°, Fig. S5), with a uniform distribution indicating homogeneous strain distribution; the 0Al steel showed 1.16° with inhomogeneous red/yellow patches near the crack.

Retained austenite content of the 1.3Al,2 h steel is 1.8 % (0.8 % higher than the 0Al steel); the toughness improvement is attributed mainly to NiAl cluster dispersion rather than the retained-austenite increase.

NiAl cluster lattice parameter (~2.882 nm) closely matches the martensitic matrix (~2.866 nm), giving a lattice mismatch of only ~0.5 %; Mo and Cr atoms expand the matrix lattice and further reduce the mismatch, lowering the nucleation barrier.

The abstract reports the 1.3Al steel overall exhibits an ultimate tensile strength of ~1.9 GPa, total elongation ~15 %, U-notch impact absorption energy ~80 J and a fracture toughness of 108 MPa·m^1/2.
